 Intern - Software Engineering
 About the role 
 
• We are seeking a System Software Intern for a three-month internship to support the development and optimization of Lyte’s build infrastructure, CI/CD pipelines, and production automation. This is a hands-on DevOps-focused role where you will work directly with our Jenkins and GitLab pipeline infrastructure, build automation tooling, and help streamline the development and deployment workflows used by our hardware, firmware, and software teams. You will work alongside experienced engineers on real production challenges and have the opportunity to see your work directly improve engineering efficiency and velocity across the company. What you'll do 
 
• Develop and maintain CI/CD pipelines in Jenkins (Groovy-based declarative and scripted pipelines) and GitLab CI 
• Write and refactor Jenkins shared libraries in Groovy to standardize build, test, and release stages across projects 
• Build and maintain automation for software builds, regression testing, and hardware-in-the-loop test stations using Python and Bash 
• Manage and improve build/test infrastructure: Jenkins agents, Docker-based build environments, artifact management, and pipeline reliability 
• Help migrate and consolidate pipelines between Jenkins and GitLab CI, improving speed, caching, and maintainability 
• Develop monitoring, logging, and pipeline-health dashboards to improve visibility into build and test infrastructure 
• Troubleshoot build failures, flaky tests, and environment issues across embedded (PetaLinux/FPGA) and application software targets 
• Document pipeline architecture, deployment procedures, and operational best practices 
• Collaborate with hardware, firmware, and software teams in a fast-paced, distributed environment Required Qualifications 
 
• Currently pursuing a degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field 
• Proficiency in Python and/or Bash scripting 
• Working knowledge of Linux/Unix environments and command-line tools 
• Familiarity with Git and standard version-control workflows (branching, merge requests, code review) 
• Basic understanding of CI/CD concepts (build, test, artifact, deploy stages) 
• Hands-on exposure to Jenkins (pipelines, Groovy, shared libraries) and/or GitLab CI/CD 
• Experience with Groovy or willingness to learn it for Jenkins pipeline development 
• Strong problem-solving skills, intellectual curiosity, and the ability to pick up new tools quickly Preferred Qualifications 
 
• Experience with Docker containers for reproducible build/test environments 
• Exposure to embedded Linux (Yocto/PetaLinux) or cross-compilation toolchains 
• Knowledge of monitoring/observability stacks (Prometheus, Grafana, ELK) 
• Personal, open-source, or coursework projects involving automation or infrastructure Benefits (subject to location and local regulations) 
 
• Competitive salary and equity  
• Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage  
• 401(k) retirement plan  
• Flexible vacation and time-off policy  
• Collaborative, fast-paced, and inclusive work environment  
• Opportunity to work on cutting-edge technologies with a highly cross-functional team  
 About Lyte 
 Lyte builds perception systems for Physical AI operating in complex environments. The company combines custom silicon, integrated sensors, and software into a unified platform for robotics, mobility, and next-generation automation. Lyte is headquartered in Sunnyvale, California, with a global presence. For more information, visit www.lyte.ai 

 If you’re excited about building impactful technology in a dynamic, hands-on environment, we’d love to hear from you! 

 Apply now

role: Photonics Data Engineer Intern - Data Management
jd:
Summary 

 The Photonics team at QuEra pioneers cutting-edge photonic chips for integration into neutral-atom quantum computers. QuEra Computing Inc. seeks a Photonics Data Engineer Intern to develop an AI-powered data infrastructure that supports our design, fabrication, and testing workflows. You'll develop tools that transform raw measurement and metrology data into actionable insights, directly informing how we design better photonic chips faster for large-scale neutral atom quantum computers. We are looking for the Photonics Data Engineer Intern to join us for Winter 2027.

 Responsibilities 

• AI-powered Data Infrastructure: Develop an AI-powered data management infrastructure for photonic integrated circuit (PIC) design, fabrication, and testing workflows. 

• Automation and Tooling: Write Python functions and utilities to automate data ingestion, cleaning, and organization across multiple data sources. 

• Performance Analysis Pipelines: Build analysis pipelines to extract key device performance metrics (e.g., insertion loss, extinction ratio, bandwidth, yield).  Analyze fabrication metrology datasets from multiple foundries and correlate findings with device performance to identify process-performance relationships. 

• Cross-functional Collaboration: Work with other photonics engineers to define data schemas and best practices for reproducible design and testing workflows. 

• Documentation: Document data infrastructure and analysis workflows for long-term team use. 
 
 Qualifications 

• Currently pursuing or recently completed a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Physics, Mathematics, or a related discipline. 

• Strong proficiency in Python programming, with hands-on experience using AI and data science libraries including PyTorch, NumPy, SciPy, and Pandas, and familiarity with workflow automation tools. 

• Working knowledge of data storage formats, database design principles, and data analysis and visualization frameworks. 

• Proven track record of leveraging Python and AI tools to tackle challenging problems in science and physics. 

• Strong analytical mindset with exceptional problem-solving capabilities. 

• Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively across multidisciplinary teams. 

• Clear evidence of self-motivation and the ability to drive independent projects to completion. 

• While a deep background in quantum physics is not a prerequisite, a solid understanding of computer science and mathematics in the context of physical simulation and experimental analysis is required. 
 
 On-site internship. There is no relocation offered for this role. 

 QuEra is committed to cultivating a diverse work environment and is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We highly value diversity in our current and future employees and do not discriminate (including in our hiring and promotion practices) based on race, religion, color, national origin, gender, gender expression, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability status, or any other characteristic protected by law.
fit_why: Photonics physics/PyTorch/SciPy data work; no photonics exposure, weak fit

About OpenSesame 

 OpenSesame is the trusted partner for Workforce Reinvention in the age of AI. OpenSesame delivers integrated software, curated and customizable content, and expert services – embedded into existing learning, HR, and work systems – to help organizations expand their human+AI potential and thrive through change.

 Learn more: www.opensesame.com/about 

 Internship Overview 

 OpenSesame seeks passionate, driven students and new graduates who already use AI to build and solve problems to join our paid summer internship program. You’ll gain hands-on experience at a fast-growing, remote-first B2B SaaS company developing AI-powered products that help organizations upskill their people and fuel long-term growth.

 As an intern, you’ll collaborate with experienced teammates across the company to help shape the future of OpenSesame. You’ll work on meaningful projects that bring new ideas to life, strengthen the customer experience, and help customers achieve success.

 AI is how we work here, not a side topic. You’ll have access to AI tools, including Claude, and we’ll encourage you to use them to research, prototype, analyze, and build. You’ll explore how AI and data can inform strategy, improve customer outcomes, and shape the future of learning technology, and see how human-centered design and AI innovation combine to create products with global impact.

 Intern AI Hackathon 

 As part of your internship you will have the opportunity to participate in our first intern AI hackathon this summer. You’ll team up with interns from other departments to pitch, build with AI, and present a working product idea that improves how OpenSesame works or serves customers.

 About the Team 

 At OpenSesame, our Engineering Team is the creative force behind the cutting-edge solutions that bring our mission to life. Guided by Extreme Programming (XP) principles, we thrive on collaboration, pair programming, and iterative development to deliver reliable, scalable, and impactful technologies.

 Our engineers—spanning software development, DevOps, and data operations—partner across teams to tackle real-world challenges, designing and building tools that adapt to the ever-changing needs of our customers. We’re an AI-forward team, integrating artificial intelligence and automation into our products and internal systems to improve efficiency, insight, and scalability.

 Whether developing new product features, enhancing our infrastructure, or leveraging AI to optimize workflows, we’re fueled by a passion for innovation and a culture of continuous learning. Together, we’re redefining what’s possible in eLearning technology!

 Performance Objectives 

 By 2 Weeks 

• Pair program with team members to gain hands-on experience and learn our engineering, DevOps, and deployment practices. 

• Participate in team discussions about tools, technologies, and AI-driven innovations while contributing to brainstorming sessions. 

• Begin learning the technologies we use—such as TypeScript, React, Terraform, AWS, and CI/CD systems—through direct collaboration with engineers across software and DevOps. 
 
 By 30 Days 

• Work on individual and team projects, contributing to production-ready code, infrastructure, or automation tools that may include AI-powered solutions. 

• Actively participate in all team meetings and events to understand how different engineering disciplines collaborate to deliver intelligent, data-driven solutions. 

• Suggest improvements to processes, workflows, or AI-enabled tools based on your early observations and experiences. 
 
 By 60 Days 

• Take ownership of individual tasks and contribute independently to ongoing engineering, DevOps, or AI-related projects. 

• Support efforts to enhance system reliability, scalability, and automation through the integration of AI and modern engineering practices. 

• Share insights and knowledge about emerging technologies—especially in AI, automation, and infrastructure—helping foster team learning and continuous improvement. 
 
 Application and Creative Project 

 Before you start, check out our Creative Project guide . It walks through what we're looking for below in more detail.

 To apply, submit one application, which includes a link to your creative project. We want to see how you think and what you've built, so your creative project must be a video (5 minutes or less), shared as a YouTube link (unlisted is fine). Applications without a working YouTube link will not be reviewed.

 We care more about your curiosity and how you think than a polished result, so don't let your experience level stop you from applying.

 You can talk to the camera, or walk us through slides, a demo, or a screen recording. How you show it is up to you. In your video, please cover:

• How do you see OpenSesame fitting into your career journey or long-term goals? 

• What strengths, skills, or perspectives do you bring to OpenSesame to make an impact and contribute to our mission? 

• Show us something you've built with AI. What problem did you solve, and what excites you about where AI is taking learning and work?

• Haven't built anything with AI yet? Make something today! Try an AI tool, experiment with a new idea, and show us or walk us through how you did it. 

• Feel free to share something from your personal life, work, school, or anywhere else. Share whatever feels right to you. 

 We're drawn to curiosity, creativity, growth mindset and authentic expression. Keep it concise and focused. 

 Not selected for this role? You're still in the running. We'll review your application for alignment with our other open internships. If we see a potential fit, we'll reach out to you directly. 

 Additional Program Details 

 Application closes: Sunday, February 14th, 2027

 Program dates: Anticipated start June 17, 2027 through August 28th, 2027. We can adjust up to two weeks earlier for students returning to school before the program concludes.

 Commitment: Full-time (40 hours/week)

 Eligibility and location: Must be a current student enrolled in a college/university program or have graduated within the past 12 months (undergraduate, postgraduate, or associate programs accepted). This position is fully remote and can be based anywhere in the U.S.

 Compensation: $25 an hour

 Equipment: Interns must have a personal computer with specs suitable for the work and access to consistent high-speed internet during working hours.

 Opportunities and expectations: OpenSesame’s internship program is immersive and growth-focused, pairing each intern with a dedicated mentor and offering meaningful, hands-on projects that make an impact. You’ll also take part in professional development sessions, networking opportunities, the intern hackathon, and book club discussions, receive volunteer time off to give back to your community, and gain full access to our course catalog for your own learning and development.

 Interview process: After the application review, selected candidates will be invited to a virtual OpenSesame webinar to learn more about our company, culture, and internship program. Following the event, selected candidates will move forward to interviews with the hiring manager and team for the department they’re being considered for.

 Equal Employment Opportunity: OpenSesame is an Equal Employment Opportunity and Affirmative Action employer that values and welcomes diversity. We do not discriminate on the basis of various legally protected characteristics, including criminal history, and strive to provide reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities. We prioritize safety and security and may use your information accordingly, and you can contact us for assistance or accommodations during the job application process. For more information on our Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion initiatives, click here.

 CPRA (California candidates): When you submit your application, OpenSesame may collect and use your personal information in accordance with our privacy policy and the CPRA. This may include personal details and employment history, and will only be used for employment-related purposes. We may share this information with third-party service providers, but we will not sell it to third parties. If you have any questions or concerns, please contact us, and for more information on your rights under the CPRA, refer to our privacy policy or the California Attorney General’s website.
